newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on weakening baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on weakening baht.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to ease on Monday as investors nervously eye the weakening baht which continues to devalue stocks, analysts said.
The baht weakened to 30.40/30.80 per dollar onshore early on Monday against 30.00/30.60 late on Friday, effectively lowering the value of stocks in dollar terms.
The SET Index fell sharply on Friday dropping 20.78 points to 628.55 as the baht fell to record lows against the dollar. The SET 50 index ended down 2.07 to 47.12.
"I think the currency exchange situation will influence the stock market," said an analyst at a Bangkok Bank affiliate.
"If the currency touches 31 I think it's a dangerous sign for the economy ... Today I think the (stock) market is going down again," he said.
On a positive note underweight funds may continue to buy stocks on fears of missing out on a short term rebound should an IMF or Japanese bailout be secured this week, analysts said.
The banking sector is a concern as corporates clients report losses from foreign borrowings and tight liquidity is begiining to affect some smaller banks, analysts said.
